","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/horowhenua-district-council_members-choice-award-finalists-2026-activity-7462299880175169536-x45u"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Horowhenua District Council","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/horowhenua-district-council"},"datePublished":"2026-05-14T04:01:59.854Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/horowhenua-district-council_horowhenua-district-council-has-reached-an-activity-7460539889890213888-kRaR","text":"Horowhenua District Council has reached an important milestone in the transformation of Levin’s town centre, with detailed design drawings received for the Levin War Memorial Hall development.

Mayor Bernie Wanden says the project reflects a strong blend of community feedback, future-focused design, and respect for Levin’s heritage.

“This is a project that honours our past while creating something meaningful for future generations. It’s about storytelling through design, retaining what matters to our community while opening up new opportunities for connection, activity, and growth.”

The detailed designs, prepared by Athfield Architects Ltd on behalf of The Wellington Company., incorporate key themes raised through community engagement, including onsite carparking, communal amenity space that will create a more inviting and connected town centre environment.

Group Manager Community Vision and Delivery David McCorkindale says the development is a cornerstone of the Levin Town Centre Transformation.
“We heard clearly from our community, and their aspiration is reflected in The Wellington Company’s designs. From accessible public spaces to thoughtful integration of hospitality and residential living, this is about creating a vibrant, connected heart for Levin.”

The proposal retains the footprint of the existing War Memorial Hall while introducing new elements that bring the space to life, including a town square and plaza, laneway terraces, and a mix of hospitality offerings such as a café and shared hospitality and dining spaces. Two hospitality providers are expected to activate the precinct, alongside approximately 20 new residential units.

Design features also incorporate elements of the existing building, including the use of original windows and the addition of mezzanine doors, helping to carry the story of the site forward.

“This is just one piece of the town centre transformation” McCorkindale says. “It’s one of several interdependent projects that together will reshape Levin’s town centre into a place where people want to spend time, do business, and connect.”

Council officers have until 21 May to confirm that the design conditions of the contract have been satisfied. Once confirmed, resource and building consent applications will be lodged to determine whether the development can proceed to construction in its current form.

If consent is granted, construction is expected to begin within three months of that milestone, with the project currently on track for completion by 31 December 2028.

Mayor Wanden says Council is committed to maintaining momentum while continuing to keep the community informed.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="feed-reshare-content__commentary">This week I had the privilege of joining <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/horowhenua-district-council?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card_reshare-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Horowhenua District Council</a>’s Youth Voice to talk about the magic, power and importance of youth participation in decision-making ✨🪄🦸

We unpacked how young people can make sure their voices are heard on the decisions that affect them, their mates, and the communities they care about. We also explored the principles of meaningful youth participation and used Hart’s Ladder as a tool to test whether young people are genuinely involved — or whether we are accidentally wandering into tokenism territory. Side note: young people know the difference 😉

This group is special. They are thoughtful, sharp, passionate and clearly determined to have their say on the matters that matter to them.

Huge credit to our Community Development Team for bringing together such a meaningful day of learning, activation and rangatahi voice in action.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">We’re feeling pretty proud e te whānau!

Ngā mihi nui to:
Beca, sponsor of the Placemaking Award
Our iwi and community partners who stood alongside us
And our incredible staff and wider network making this happen every day

This recognition reflects what matters most to us:
→ Strong partnerships

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Horowhenua District Council has reached an important milestone in the transformation of Levin’s town centre, with detailed design drawings received for the Levin War Memorial Hall development.

Mayor Bernie Wanden says the project reflects a strong blend of community feedback, future-focused design, and respect for Levin’s heritage.

“This is a project that honours our past while creating something meaningful for future generations. It’s about storytelling through design, retaining what matters to our community while opening up new opportunities for connection, activity, and growth.”

The detailed designs, prepared by <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/athfield-architects-ltd?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>Athfield Architects Ltd</a> on behalf of <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/company/the-wellington-company-asset-management-limited?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>The Wellington Company</a>., incorporate key themes raised through community engagement, including onsite carparking, communal amenity space that will create a more inviting and connected town centre environment.

Group Manager Community Vision and Delivery David McCorkindale says the development is a cornerstone of the Levin Town Centre Transformation.
“We heard clearly from our community, and their aspiration is reflected in The Wellington Company’s designs. From accessible public spaces to thoughtful integration of hospitality and residential living, this is about creating a vibrant, connected heart for Levin.”

The proposal retains the footprint of the existing War Memorial Hall while introducing new elements that bring the space to life, including a town square and plaza, laneway terraces, and a mix of hospitality offerings such as a café and shared hospitality and dining spaces. Two hospitality providers are expected to activate the precinct, alongside approximately 20 new residential units.

Design features also incorporate elements of the existing building, including the use of original windows and the addition of mezzanine doors, helping to carry the story of the site forward.

“This is just one piece of the town centre transformation” McCorkindale says. “It’s one of several interdependent projects that together will reshape Levin’s town centre into a place where people want to spend time, do business, and connect.”

Council officers have until 21 May to confirm that the design conditions of the contract have been satisfied. Once confirmed, resource and building consent applications will be lodged to determine whether the development can proceed to construction in its current form.

If consent is granted, construction is expected to begin within three months of that milestone, with the project currently on track for completion by 31 December 2028.

Mayor Wanden says Council is committed to maintaining momentum while continuing to keep the community informed.
“We are delighted that the Wellington Company have embraced the challenge of considering the history and identity of the space and are looking to create a development that will act as a catalyst for the transformation of the Levin Town Centre.”</p>
